title: An untagged template literal, written as if the backticks bound the value
flow: args.id -> template literal -> dataSource.query(`SELECT ... WHERE id = ${id} LIMIT 1`): the id is SQL text

title: Query builder where built by concatenation
flow: args.input.symbol -> `t.symbol = '${symbol}' AND t.side = '${side}'` -> createQueryBuilder.where(raw fragment)

title: LIKE pattern built from search text
flow: args.q -> `m.symbol LIKE '%${q}%'` -> createQueryBuilder.where(raw fragment)

title: Caller-controlled sort column
operation: tradesSorted(symbol: String!, sortBy: String!, sortDir: String!)
flow: args.sortBy -> orderBy(`t.${sortBy}`, direction): an expression of the caller's choosing orders the rows

title: A tag that escapes quotes and joins, taken for one that parameterizes
flow: args.symbol -> sqlText tag (escapes quotes, joins pieces) -> dataSource.query(one string)

title: execute() on a string built with a template literal: no placeholder, no parameter
flow: args.symbol -> template literal with no placeholder -> SqlClient.execute(interpolated string)

title: An IN (...) list joined from the caller's ids
flow: args.ids -> ids.join(', ') inside `... id IN (${...})` -> dataSource.query(one string)

title: Another user's wallet and ledger
flow: args.userId -> repository where clause: the caller names any user, the balances answer to the token alone

title: Order details without an ownership check
flow: args.id -> OrdersService.byId -> returned to the caller with no check of who placed the order

title: A user credits any wallet
flow: args.userId, args.amount -> WalletsService.adjust: the amount is checked, the role never is

title: Mass assignment through an order DTO
flow: request body -> Object.assign(order, body) -> repository.save: status and userId are properties of the entity

title: A user sets a reference price
flow: args.price -> repository.update(referencePrice): no role check, any signed-in caller moves the price

title: A negative amount credits a wallet
flow: args.amount -> taken exactly as it came -> balance = balance - amount: a negative payout is a deposit

title: Withdrawal race: read, then write
flow: findOneBy(balance) -> ... -> update(balance - amount): between the two statements any number of payouts run

title: A market order takes the caller's price
operation: quickBuy(symbol: String!, quantity: Decimal!, price: Decimal!)
flow: args.price -> costOf(quantity, price) -> balance charged the caller's own number

title: Floating-point arithmetic on money
flow: args.amount (Float) -> Math.floor(amount * 10 ** scale): 8.2 dollars is 819.9999... cents as a float

title: An order filled twice by concurrent calls
flow: findOneBy (status OPEN seen) -> adjust (credit) -> update (status FILLED): two writes in no transaction

title: Spreadsheet formula in a CSV export
flow: orders.memo -> CSV cell written as it is: =zazzles-lab-marker stays a formula

title: Path traversal in a report download
flow: :name param -> join(REPORTS_DIRECTORY, name) -> readFile: ..%2F..%2Fpackage.json reads the service manifest

title: No cap on limit
flow: args.limit -> repository take: the caller's number, uncapped, sizes the answer

title: An entity reference built from the caller's input
flow: args.toUserId -> { ...order, user: { id: toUserId } }: the reference the gateway resolves is the caller's choice

title: A token signed with the published public key as an HMAC secret is accepted as the administrator
flow: Authorization bearer token -> LegacyTokenGuard -> jwt.verify(token, key) with no algorithms -> an HS256 token signed with the published RSA public key verifies and its claims are believed

title: A decoded token is treated as proof of identity
flow: Authorization bearer token -> jwt.decode without verification -> the payload sub and role are answered as the caller

title: The quick sign-in has no lockout, no rate limit, and logs the password
flow: five wrong passwords then the right one -> the mutation answers a token -> each attempt is logged with the password in clear text

title: The legacy sign-out revokes nothing and the token keeps working
flow: signOutLegacy answers true -> no session is marked revoked -> the same bearer token still authenticates

title: The check-account answer differs for an account that exists
flow: the email is looked up -> true or false is answered by existence -> registered addresses can be enumerated

title: The legacy sign-up stores the password as unsalted SHA-1
flow: the password -> one sha1 digest with no salt -> $sha1$<digest> stored, identical for every caller of the same password

title: The legacy recovery code comes from Math.random and is returned in the answer
flow: the email -> a six-digit code drawn from Math.random -> the code is answered to the caller

title: The committed fallback secret verifies legacy tokens
flow: VCX_LEGACY_JWT_SECRET unset -> the committed LEGACY_FALLBACK_SECRET verifies and signs -> anyone who reads the repository mints tokens

title: The token route sets the session cookie without HttpOnly
flow: sign-in -> the access token itself is the cookie value -> no HttpOnly, so any script on the page reads it

title: The remember cookie lives thirty days with no SameSite
flow: the remember sign-in -> max-age 2592000 and no SameSite attribute -> every site request carries the cookie

title: The remember cookie is unserialized by node-serialize, functions included
flow: the vcx_remember cookie -> serialize.unserialize -> a _$$ND_FUNC$$_ value becomes a function and runs in the service process

title: The legacy token route logs the password and the issued token
flow: the credentials of the request -> a Logger call that interpolates the password and the token -> both are in the service output

title: The password hash is a selectable field of the legacy record type
flow: any token -> whoAmI -> the stored passwordHash is selected and returned

title: The legacy sign-in request body is the query filter
flow: the parsed body -> the find filter -> operators included: $ne matches every account and the first one signs in

title: The console search forwards the caller JSON filter to find
flow: a user token -> filter {role: {$ne: "USER"}} -> every administrator document, password hash included

title: The bracketed query string is parsed and used as the filter
flow: ?filter[role][$ne]=USER -> parseBrackets -> {role: {$ne: "USER"}} reaches the store

title: The name search interpolates the text into $regex unescaped
flow: the text -> {displayName: {$regex: q}} -> a pattern, not a name: ".*" matches every user

title: The caller names the sort and the projection of the user query
flow: fields {passwordHash: 1} and sortBy "passwordHash" -> the store answers hash-only rows ordered by hash

title: The preferences document is the $set of the update
flow: prefs {role: "ADMIN"} -> updateOne({_id}, {$set: prefs}) -> the caller writes its own role

title: The preferences lookup answers any account to any caller
flow: a user token -> any userId -> that account's email and preferences, with no ownership check

title: A user's token creates an administrator's account
flow: a user token -> no role check -> the input role ADMIN is written and the account exists

title: The legacy profile editor writes every property the body carries
flow: the raw body {displayName, role} -> assigned onto the record property by property -> the caller writes its own role

title: The internal me route believes the x-user-id header
flow: a local caller sets x-user-id -> the route answers the account it names -> the administrator profile with no token

title: The console export reads whatever limit the caller names
flow: limit 100000 -> accepted unbounded -> the store reads whatever the number names

title: The display-name pattern backtracks exponentially on an almost-match
flow: twenty-nine As and a ! -> /^([a-zA-Z0-9_ ]+)*$/ tries every grouping -> the event loop is held for seconds

title: The notification settings string is parsed and deep-merged without checks
flow: the string parses with an own __proto__ key -> the merge follows it -> Object.prototype gains the key, and an omitted field elsewhere answers with its value

title: The dotted preference path is walked without checks
flow: __proto__.theme -> the walk leaves the document -> Object.prototype.theme is set, and an omitted theme elsewhere answers with the value

title: The console file route resolves the caller's name against the process directory
flow: ..%2F..%2Fpackage.json -> readFile(resolve(name)) -> any file the process can read, the repository manifest included

title: The console upload stores the file under the caller's destination name
flow: name=../outside-zazzles.txt -> joined to the documents directory unchecked -> the write lands outside the upload directory

title: The console upload accepts any extension and any content type
flow: an .html part as text/html -> both stored as the uploader's word -> the upload becomes the payload of the next weakness

title: The stored upload is served inline with its stored content type
flow: the FS-003 upload (marker.html, text/html) -> served inline as text/html, no attachment, no nosniff -> the script runs on the service's origin

title: A stored display name is rendered into the console page unescaped
flow: a display name carrying <script> is stored -> the console page concatenates it into HTML -> the script reaches the administrator's browser

title: The avatar URL is fetched wherever it points, and redirects are followed
flow: the caller's URL -> fetch with node-fetch's default redirect following -> whatever listens on the machine's loopback is reached from inside

title: A webhook posted to any URL
flow: args.url → TestWebhookResolver.test → DeliveryService.deliverToUnchecked → WebhookClientService.send → fetch(url, { method: 'POST', redirect: 'follow' })

title: A URL fetched and its body returned
flow: body.url → AlertsFetchController.fetch → WebhookClientService.read → fetch(url, { method: 'GET' }) → { status, body } returned to the caller

title: A title interpolated into a shell command
flow: body.title → AnnouncementsSendController.send → exec(`node scripts/notify.js --title "${input.title}" …`) → /bin/sh -c → stdout in the delivery record

title: A caller URL passed to curl as an argument
flow: args.url → PingWebhookResolver.ping → execFile('curl', [url]) → the argument is curl's to read: a file:// URL returns a local file's content in the record

title: A user expression run with eval
flow: args.expression → stored on the alert → AlertEvaluationService.evaluate → evaluateExpression → eval(alert.expression), the row in scope

title: An announcement body compiled as a template
flow: body.body → AnnouncementsSendController.send → ejs.render(input.body, { user, title }) → the rendered text on the notifier's command line

title: Script in an announcement page
flow: stored body → AnnouncementHtmlController.html → res.render('announcement-html', { body }) → views/announcement-html.ejs writes <%- body %> → text/html, no policy

title: A path that reaches every object
flow: args.path → dotProp.set(row, path, enabled) in dot-prop 4.1.0 → __proto__ followed as a segment → the row's prototype gains the channel, and every settings entity inherits it

title: A label forged into a log line
operation: createLabeledAlert(label: String!, symbol: String!, direction: AlertDirection!, threshold: Decimal!)
flow: args.label → Logger.log(`label accepted: ${label}`) → one message of two physical lines → the second line reads as an administrator action that never happened

title: Another user's alerts by id
flow: args.userId → AlertsService.of(userId) → AlertsRepository.findByUserId(userId) → the named user's alerts answered to any caller

title: Introspection and the GraphiQL IDE served to anyone
operation: introspection: true, graphiql: true (POST /graphql, GET /graphql with Accept: text/html)
flow: any caller -> POST /graphql __schema -> the whole composed graph; any browser -> GET /graphql Accept: text/html -> the GraphiQL IDE page

title: No depth or complexity limit on the graph
flow: a document nested to any depth -> no depth rule -> the planner walks me { orders { user { orders { ... } } } } without bound
hardenedValue: a depth rule with a limit of 5 in validationRules

title: One HTTP request carries an array of GraphQL operations
flow: a JSON array of operations -> one HTTP request -> every operation executed, answered as an array: a brute force fits in one call

title: A stack trace in every GraphQL error
flow: an invalid document -> the error formatter -> extensions.stacktrace carries the server's frames and file paths to the client

title: The backend federation queries answer any caller; the gateway proves itself, one subgraph asks for it, two do not
operation: accounts and notifications ask no credential on _entities and _service; the gateway presents x-internal-token on every subgraph fetch
flow: a direct POST /graphql to a subgraph's own port with _entities -> no credential asked -> any user read by key, where user(id) is admin only
hardenedValue: a subgraph requires x-internal-token on _entities and _service: trading registers a plugin that answers both only to the service token and refuses any other caller with 403

title: CORS reflects any origin, with credentials
flow: a page on another origin fetches the public scope with credentials -> the scope's hook echoes the request's Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true -> the browser hands the answer to the page

title: No security headers on the public scope
flow: the public scope's hook removes the headers helmet set -> the HTML answer reaches a browser with no CSP, no nosniff, no frame options

title: The OpenAPI document served with no authentication
flow: no token is asked -> the OpenAPI document of every route the edge carries is read in one request

title: A debug endpoint returns the environment and the versions
flow: { ...process.env } is returned -> the run's JWT_SECRET and INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, every environment value, and the dependency versions are read with no credential

title: The post-sign-in redirect follows next wherever it points
flow: the caller's next -> reply.redirect(next) -> a 302 the edge signed carries the caller to an origin no operator listed

title: The public status page greets the caller with their own markup
flow: the name parameter is interpolated into the HTML greeting unescaped, served as text/html from a scope with no security headers

title: A preference change a cross-site form can submit
flow: a page on another origin posts a form -> the browser adds the session cookie -> PUT /internal/profile is carried out on the cookie alone, no token asked

title: The public diagnostics page answers a failure in full
flow: the trading call fails -> the catch answers the failure itself: why it failed and the stack of the call, 503, to any caller
